prompts:
Use case: sketch-to-render, stylized-concept.
Create ONE polished, wide panoramic game-level watercolor scene illustration, approximately 2:1 landscape. This is Level 06 “Greenhouse Seedbeds” for a poetic microscopic 2D platform puzzle game. Transform the supplied schematic into a believable playable environment.
INPUT 1 = layout reference ONLY: use the large central scene rectangle in the flowchart, IGNORE all text, legends, inset, panels, and arrows. INPUT 2 = approved art-style reference ONLY: retain its illustrated watercolor, subtly outlined organic architecture, subdued distant layers, and tiny luminous spirit; do NOT reuse its pool layout.
CAMERA: exact front-on orthographic side elevation perpendicular to the greenhouse wall. All playable foreground ledge top edges are straight horizontal and parallel to the bottom image edge. No isometric view, no oblique camera, no perspective ramp platforms. A little depth is allowed ONLY in distant greenhouse architecture.
SCENE: the gap between two enormous old greenhouse seedbeds, seen by a tiny light spirit. A deep drainage trench below separates the left and right banks. Abandoned pale sage-painted greenhouse ribs, cracked foggy glass panes and roof, faded whitewashed brick dwarf walls, silhouettes of enormous seedlings, fern leaves, old terracotta pots, small drooping roots. Soft late afternoon ivory sunlight, tranquil hopeful fairy-tale atmosphere. Rich foreground watercolor with paper grain, warm ochre terra cotta and muted olive green; BACKGROUND gently softened, reduced contrast and paler watercolor, still recognizably a greenhouse. No white fog washout. Keep foreground and background fully consistent in materials, lighting, scale, and weathering.
STATE: show ONE coherent final upper-light-route state, with the nursery tray RAISED. No duplicate or ghost tray. No second state or insets. The low route is OFF and must NOT be drawn.
PLACEMENT as approximate percentages of full frame, with y from top:
- LEFT LOWER A: broad horizontal mossy brick seedbed rim at y85%, spanning x0–32%; entrance from an old pump inspection opening at bottom-left. A pivoting irregular silvered greenhouse-glass shard at (14%,79%), on a small worn wood-and-brass gardening clamp actually attached to the rim, not a freestanding household mirror. One tiny ivory flame-headed spirit near A, big head tiny body, entire figure about 3–4% picture height. Subtle warm trailing ember particles behind the hair.
- LEFT UPPER C: a short salvaged translucent glass nursery shelf at x20–33%, y29%, attached to seedbed posts with brackets. Its walkable top is horizontal. A second adjustable glass-shard mirror at (24%,22%) is physically fixed to this shelf edge; it has a tiny seedpod-shaped adjustment handle.
- CENTRAL P: exactly ONE shallow terracotta nursery tray hanging at HIGH position x47–60%, horizontal floor at y30%. Two visibly braided brown ropes hang vertically to its two ends from modest worn timber pulley wheels attached to the greenhouse crossbeam. A small FIXED silvery reflector at (53%,26%) on a LOW stem at the tray's edge; it belongs to the tray and moves with it. A few sprouts/moss at the sides, clear standing space in the center. The tray is visibly a gardening object, not an elevator cage. Hanging ropes are matte brown, clearly different from glowing light.
- LOWER CENTRAL K: a SMALL fixed curtain-release lever/cord latch at (50%,90%) bolted into the exposed back wall of the trench. It does NOT hang from the high tray. In this state the low tray landing is empty and the latch is visibly unreachable from the banks. To its right, two short horizontal weathered nursery shelf/terracotta fragment steps at (63%,88%) and (67%,85%), fixed to the trench wall by roots/brackets; they are small isolated footholds, never a bridge across the whole trench. These are the re-entry steps for the lower beam in another state.
- G: a small old opaque green growing shade at (19%,54%) is ROLLED UP, with a thin brown drawcord routed against the back wall to fixed K below. No glowing linkage lines.
- F and RIGHT BAFFLE: at about x39% and x69%, two narrow, aged opaque greenhouse shade-cloth/wooden baffles descend from the overhead seedbed framework to y74%, ending ABOVE the inactive lower-route height. Each has ONE tiny horizontal slit at the appropriate upper light height (left slit about y24%, right slit about y24%). Integrate them naturally as worn plant-growing shade screens edged with a little ivy and old clamps; no sterile abstract rectangles, no floating sci-fi gates. Their tops join the overhead structure so they do not form new walkable ledges. Correct upper rays pass through the slits, never through solid material.
- RIGHT LOWER B: second broad mossy seedbed rim x81–100%, y85%. A brown rope-winding gardening winch at (94%,82%) fixed to the wood/brick bed edge. Its actual brown rope routes up along the right post to the two pulley wheels supporting P. Leave an accessible standing area beside the winch; no disconnected oversized machine.
- RIGHT UPPER D: old horizontal seedbed shelf x80–100%, y29%. Adjustable last reflector at (83%,22%), firmly attached to a weathered nursery rack with an accessible handle. To its right, at x92–100%, show ONLY a curved portion of the enormous creature's pale ivory rib/flank disappearing beneath greenhouse foundations and plants; layered organic scales, soft living form, NOT a rock pile, not a full animal. The single target scale at (94%,12%) has a smoky gray body with a warm golden illuminated center. Next to the shelf a leaf-curtained opening leads into the next level.
ONE LIGHT PATH ONLY, continuous, no branches: a crack in greenhouse glazing at (4%,43%) sends a warm narrow sunbeam diagonally down to A(14,79), reflected steeply up to C(24,22), then slightly down-right through the left shade slit to P's raised fixed mirror(53,26), then slightly up-right through the right shade slit to D(83,22), then up-right to the creature's target scale(94,12). Beam has a warm gold halo and bright core, clearly visible but not a giant laser tube. Mirror planes must face their incoming and outgoing rays. No horizontal beam between A and B in this pictured state.
INTEGRATION AND READABILITY: foreground mechanics share believable fittings, contact shadows, moss, and watercolor texture with the seedbeds. Slightly darker contour and a restrained warm-white glint on interactive handles and walkable edges make them readable; no heavy neon aura. Do not plant foliage over landing edges or beam slits. Behind the action, glasshouse foliage stays pale and soft. A small amount of framing foliage can occur at the outer edges only, not obscure the puzzle.
No text, letters, numbered labels, arrows, UI, collage, schematic symbols, flat white panels, massive industrial pulley tower, multiple light sources, spare mirror routes, or duplicate protagonist. This is finished narrative game-scene concept art, not a technical diagram and not a photorealistic render.

Edit this existing greenhouse watercolor game scene. Preserve the composition, panoramic 2:1 canvas, entire environment, palette, pale soft watercolor background, sharply readable horizontal platforms, all beams and their endpoints, single raised nursery tray, two slit screens, low fixed latch and two steps, right winch, creature flank and glowing target scale. Make ONLY these three precise corrections:
1) The fixed mirror on the raised central terracotta tray, currently around 55% x / 28% y, should be a nearly HORIZONTAL flat silvered glass shard on its short stem. The incoming ray travels shallowly down-right from C and the outgoing ray shallowly up-right to D, so the reflecting plane must be near horizontal. Show it as a shallow oval/slender silver plane, almost edge-on, roughly 60 pixels wide by 10–15 pixels high at this image scale, with a restrained rim highlight. Keep its reflection point at the same location so the existing golden rays remain continuous. No additional mirrors.
2) Reduce the single flame-headed ivory spirit near the lower-left bank to approximately HALF its current height, to about 4.5–5% of total picture height, feet still at the very same floor point. Preserve the huge flame head/small body proportions, identity, watercolor rendering and faint luminous hair particles. Fill the uncovered area naturally with existing background and moss. Do not change any platform or prop scale.
3) Reposition the rolled-up GREEN SHADE BLIND that currently sits at left-middle around x20–29%, y49%. Move it up and left, to span approximately x12.5–19.7% at y37% (below-left of the upper-left glass shelf). Make this roll a little narrower to fit. IMPORTANT: the roll in its raised state must be ABOVE and to the LEFT of the diagonal A-to-C golden ray, leaving that ray completely unobstructed. If this blind were unrolled straight downward from its new roll, its fabric WOULD cross the A-to-C ray lower down; this spatial relationship is the point of the correction. Anchor the roll to the old greenhouse/seedbed support naturally. Reroute its thin non-glowing brown drawcord down the back wall to the EXISTING low central latch, keeping that latch fixed in place. Remove the old roll cleanly and restore the greenhouse glazing/foliage behind it. The drawcord lives behind the gameplay plane.
Do not alter the light route, mirror count, high position of the single tray, existing rope winch system, final ivory creature flank, side-view camera, or horizontal playable ledges. No text, arrows, overlay, numbers, or UI.

Refine the supplied finished watercolor greenhouse level concept while preserving its exact panoramic camera, soft pale watercolor background, illustration style, all greenhouse architecture, plant palette, single raised hanging tray, tiny light spirit, and single continuous upper light route. Keep the newly horizontal tray mirror and moved rolled shade. Make a final gameplay-readability correction, not a redesign.
A) Mirrors must read as reflecting the drawn rays. Lower-left mirror A: shorten its support so its reflecting center is at x14.4%, y76.7% (about 30px above its horizontal bank floor), and make its silver plane almost horizontal, just slightly higher on the right. Reconnect the SAME incoming ray from the left window and SAME outgoing ray toward C to this new slightly lower reflection point, with no extra beam. Upper-left C: keep its reflection point fixed but make the reflecting plane slope about 30 degrees upward toward the right. Right-upper D: keep its reflection point fixed but make the plane only about 15 degrees upward toward the right. These are attached garden-glass shards with normal aged fittings, not floating circles. The tray P mirror stays as it is.
B) Adjust ONLY the low fixed maintenance latch K and its two wall steps to match the tiny spirit. Move K upward: its mounting plate center near x50.5%, y83.5%, lever handle around y81%. Keep its brown cord connected to the rolled blind. It is fixed to the back wall, NOT to the tray. Do not draw a second low tray. A low tray would later stop with its floor near y86%, within roughly two character-heights under the dormant lower route at y76.7%.
Move the two SMALL fixed terracotta footholds: first step spans x63–66% with a horizontal top at y83%; second spans x67–70% with a horizontal top at y80%. Their wood/root brackets attach to the wall. These sit to the right of the tray's vertical travel area and must not collide with it. Remove the old lower footholds cleanly.
C) The right LOWER bank's LEFT EDGE should be at x82% rather than its current x74%; keep the winch at its existing location around x88–90% on the remaining right bank. Extend the empty trench to this new bank edge. This leaves a visibly unjumpable gap between the last small step ending at x70% and the right bank starting at x82%. The opposite left bank, high right shelf, and all other platforms remain as they are.
D) Show a clearly readable small leaf-curtained EXIT at the far-right end of the UPPER D shelf, floor exactly level with that upper shelf, below the ivory creature flank. Leaves form a gentle arch into a shadowed green passage. The lower right area is closed greenhouse/seedbed wall, no inviting lower exit, steps or doorway bypassing the upper goal. The tiny extra metal wheel on the far-left entry door is weathered muted brown, not bright gold.
Preserve the ivory-scaled flank with only its target scale glowing, ropes matte brown versus warm gold light, exactly one tiny spirit on the left bank, exactly one nursery tray high in the middle. No extra platforms, labels, arrows, text, numbers, UI, duplicate state or new light route. Keep the beautiful watercolor environmental integration.

validation.state: P raised, G open, upper route illuminated
